profile.headline: iOS Architect with 15+ Years of Native Apple platform Design and Development Experience in Swift (including SwiftUI and Swift Concurrency) and Objective-C. I've successfully built and launched over a dozen apps.
profile.summary:
Native iOS mobile app developer and team leader who's an expert in Swift and Objective-C with a passion for user experience (UX).  I enjoy designing apps that rethink data and experiences for the small screen.  I love leading teams that utilize open-source and enterprise libraries and frameworks with high-performance native iOS code to develop apps that consume data and expose it to users in beautiful, new, and innovative ways.

I'm customer oriented and comfortable communicating through the written or spoken word, I thrive on the bleeding edge of development and technology for both large and small projects, and am more than comfortable leading and teaching others.  I work best in a team, and enjoy the social and technical aspects of working for a small and fast-moving company.

Specialty:  Native iOS development with Swift, SwiftUI, Objective-C, and UIKit utilizing design patterns and TDD.

positions.title: Sr. IOS Engineer (L5)
positions.description:
Member of the Mobile Platform Team responsible for refactoring the 10+ year old One Medical mobile app codebase into a modern SwiftUI app using a modular architecture. As part of the team charged with owning the Amazon Health mobile apps as One Medical finishes their integration into Amazon Health, we’re working to establish tools and frameworks to enable rapid feature development and iteration while maintaining software quality and app stability.
• Designed and built a reusable framework refactoring previously tightly-coupled authentication, keychain access, and device biometrics code out of the main app. Abstracted the OAuth provider using an adaptor pattern to allow a planned switch to a different vendor with minimal effort.
• Designed, prototyped, and championed an architecture for a dynamic server-driven UI that allows for
complete control of the app’s frontend from the backend, while maintaining the superior user experience
and accessibility (Dynamic Type and Voice Over) of a native SwiftUI interface. Strongly utilizing Swift
Package Manager (SPM) for code reuse and modularization.
• Defined patterns and examples for transitioning from UIKit to SwiftUI and modern Swift Concurrency while maintaining unit testable business logic, Clean Architecture, and enabling rapid UI development with Xcode Previews.
• Responsible for regularly reviewing pull requests and architectural design documents across multiple
mobile development teams to ensure Swift Concurrency, SwiftUI, and accessibility best practices, proper
software architecture, and useful and effective automated testing.
positions.insights: Skills: Swift (Programming Language) · SwiftUI · Unit Testing · Software Architecture · iOS Development · Swift Concurrency

positions.title: Freelance iOS Engineer
positions.description:
• Designed, built, and launched a SwiftUI app with a 3-layer architecture and modern Swift Concurrency for recording audio, uploading it to a server for transcription and LLM-based processing, and then dynamically displaying the results of the processing to the user. Optimized the app for background processing and uploading and to support offline scenarios.
• Designed an app architecture for a computer vision startup utilizing modern Swift Concurrency, the Vision and CoreML frameworks in a SwiftUI app. Advised on converting the initial PoC into a properly-architected and maintainable app.
• Mentored and code-reviewed junior developers at a computer vision fitness startup to improve app
performance and increase the maintainability and unit testability of the codebase.

positions.title: Principal iOS Developer
positions.description:
Designed, architected, developed, launched, and maintained a green field SwiftUI app to invigorate the
bowling experience at Bowlero Bowling Centers while attracting new bowlers.
• Built, mentored and worked with a small team of native iOS developers as both an individual contributor
and project team lead, while closely collaborating with the native Android team, UI/UX designers, product
managers, and the server-side team.

match Bowlero’s unique brand identity. Utilized Fastlane and GitHub Actions for a rich CI pipeline to track
and enforce code quality while using automated testing and code coverage reporting.
• Integrated with an event-driven backend using gRPC as a transport to provide near real-time updates to
the app while the bowler played their game in-center, in often challenging network environments.

positions.title: Lead Platform Engineer - iOS
positions.description:
Developed and maintained a native iOS app designed to “make doctors happy” and optimize their billing and documentation workflow.
• Updated the toolchain from Xcode 10 to 12, and eventually 13. Introduced formal package management
with Swift Package Manager, replacing git submodules, un-versioned pre-compiled binary libraries, and
arbitrary files copy-and-pasted from 3rd party repositories, allowing industry-required 3rd-party security
audits.
• Incrementally modernized legacy, manually memory managed Objective-C to ARC while also updating to modern syntactic sugar features like properties, boxing, and generics, which vastly improved readability and made it easier for junior-level iOS developers to understand. Introduced Swift coding standards and migrated new development to Swift, updating the few existing pieces of Swift code to Swift 5 features and idioms. Incrementally modernized UI code to use Storyboards and/or auto layout as well as adding support for Dynamic Type (one of the number one feature requests of the app).
• Introduced iOS performance and unit testing along with incrementally introducing a testable architecture. Introduced progressive-enhancement-style features and architectures using Swift’s version gating to gain the benefits of modern APIs while allowing users to continue using the app on older versions of iOS.
• Mentored the entire development team in writing high-quality, testable, and well-architected Swift code. Helped to bring a new-hire, junior developer up to productivity on the iOS codebase while also teaching the basics of test-driven development and clean code.

positions.title: Senior Software Architect
positions.description:
Developed and maintained a suite of health related iOS apps specializing in aggregating and visualizing
health data from multiple sources including 1st and 3rd party RESTful services and Apple HealthKit, CareKit, and ResearchKit.
• Introduced the team of Microsoft developers to Storyboards and Auto Layout and handled most of the
visual design to Interface Builder translation for early apps, while establishing Objective-C coding
standards and evangelizing automated testing, CI, and following the Apple HIG.
• Spearheaded and evangelized the implementation of iOS’ accessibility APIs, including Dynamic Type and Voice Over.
• Worked with a small team on-site at Apple in Cupertino prior to the Apple Watch’s general availability to
develop a WatchKit 1.0 application and have it ready for day-one launch of the watchOS app store.
• Interviewed developers to build-out the mobile development team, including interviewing and hiring for the entire native Android development team.

projects.title: Speaking Engagement - Going Offline with HTML5
projects.description:
Presented at jQuery Conference 2011: Boston -

Description: HTML5 introduces and standardizes a number of client-side caching and data storage mechanisms, specifically cache manifest, indexed database, and web storage. We'll take a tour of the available JavaScript APIs and explore their use in building on and offline web applications, increasing in-browser performance of online-only apps, and dealing with the inconsistent network connections common to mobile devices. We'll also cover diagnosing and debugging some common pitfalls, and of course dealing with browsers that don't support the new functionality.

projects.title: Speaking Engagement - Natural Language UI Testing using Behavior Driven Development with Pavlov and QUnit
projects.description:
Presented at jQuery Conference 2011: San Francisco Bay Area - 

Description: Using concepts borrowed from the RSpec and Cucumber projects we'll explore the process of converting a stakeholder-readable design specification of a user interface feature into a QUnit test suite.

We'll use the excellent Pavlov behavioral API to to produce readable, high-level tests that describe and test the way a UI works, not the way it should be programmed. Once a few tests are written, we'll implement the feature using the typical TDD red, green, refactor approach.

Throughout the talk, all of our examples will attempt to provide a real-world implementation of TDD without boiling it down to a simple abstraction that requires too much interpretation to apply to production code.
